body: While the Arctic is thawing, Arctic relations are heating up:

. Whereas the region was once praised for its exceptional nature, remaining isolated from geopolitical tension, it has transformed into a region highly affected by them. In other words: “the Arctic is no longer the frozen and remote region it once was” (Ibrahim, 2024, para. 1).
This thesis explored the erosion of Arctic exceptionalism and Complex Interdependence,

, as defined by the Copenhagen School, during 2008-2024. The research question, How did the changing relationship between the US and Russia influence the nature of Arctic exceptionalism through mutual securitization between 2008 and 2024?, was answered by qualitatively analyzing a total of 48 documents, including four strategic policy documents, and led to the following main findings:

First, the increase of securitization went hand in hand with the sudden erosion of Arctic exceptionalism since 2014, since the securitization of geopolitical events unrelated to the Arctic allowed these events to impact Arctic relations, directly removing the exceptionalist nature of the region. This means that Arctic exceptionalism eroded across all five sectors after 2014, due to the influence of securitization. This was observable in various ways, such as the US leveraging Russian invasion of Ukraine to justify extraordinary measures against Russia in the Arctic. Moreover, even though the effects of the decreasing levels of Arctic exceptionalism and securitization were most visible in the political, military and economic domain, they rippled through to the social and environmental domain indirectly. This, since even though no direct securitization efforts were found in the latter two domains, the increased tension that accompanied securitization decreased national attention away from social- and environmental issues, by shifting attention to the other three securitized domains in both speech and strategy. This was not only visible in-text, but also in the multitude of documents, since the number of documents relatively increased after 2022, while the focus on social- and environmental issues decreased, since most speech acts revolved around securitized issues. Thus, Arctic exceptionalism eroded because geopolitical events had direct and indirect spill-over effects into the region since 2014, and securitization played a prominent role in this development, since it allowed the nations to perceive geopolitical events as a threat to Arctic security.
